  1. To add someone, fill in the Add a member form and select “Add member”. Give them the username and the temporary password; they must choose their own at first sign-in (see “Choosing your own password”).
  2. Roles: Owner has full access including the Tools and settings page. Manager has the same rights except the Tools and settings page, deletes only records they created and cannot reveal the alarm webhook key. Executor submits requests, creates and works work orders, and views everything else. Guest can only read.
  3. Use the pencil on a row to set the person’s email address and notification preferences (daily digest).
  4. Use the key on a row to reset a password. Leave the box blank to have the app generate a temporary password and show it to you once.
  5. Use the red bin to remove an account. You cannot remove your own.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Member row — Username, email (if set), a role tag, and three buttons. A line “Temporary password — must change at next sign-in” shows for people who have not yet chosen their own.
  • 2Reset password (key) — Sets a new temporary password for that person.
  • 3Member settings (pencil) — Email address and notification preferences for that person.
  • 4Add a member — Form to create an account.
  • 5Username * — The name they sign in with.
  • 6Temporary password * — At least 8 characters. Temporary: they must change it at first sign-in.
  • 7Role — Owner, Manager, Executor or Guest.
  • 8Email (optional) — Used for notifications and self-service password reset.
  • 9Add member — Creates the account.

Tools and settings: a member’s email and notification settings

Set where a person’s emails go and what they receive. Notification emails need your Owner to have configured a mail server for the app.

What to do

  1. On the member’s row select the pencil.
  2. Enter or change the email address.
  3. Tick the items to include in the person’s daily digest email: overdue work orders, warranties expiring soon, and work requests sitting unreviewed.
  4. Save.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Email — Where this person’s notification emails and reset links are sent.
  • 2Designations — Planner, Scheduler and Specialist for executors; an Executor flag for Owners and Managers (off by default). They decide who can plan, schedule and be assigned work.
  • 3Save — Stores the settings.

Tools and settings: resetting a password

If someone forgets their password and cannot use the email reset, set a new temporary one. They must change it at their next sign-in, and any devices where they were signed in are signed out.

What to do

  1. Select the key on their row.
  2. Type a temporary password, or leave the box empty to have one generated.
  3. Select “Reset password” and give the person the temporary password (a generated one is shown once).

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Temporary password — At least 8 characters; blank means generate one.
  • 2Reset password — Applies the change and signs the person out everywhere.

Tools and settings: Branding and terminology

Make the app your own: its name, logo and colours, and the words used for locations. Changes apply to everyone straight away and are included in the Excel backup.

What to do

  1. Fill in the names: Name (required), Short name (used where space is tight), Tagline (below the logo) and an optional Top-bar title.
  2. Upload a logo (PNG, JPG, SVG or WebP, up to 512 KB).
  3. Choose the four colours: primary and accent for light mode and for dark mode. Enter a hex code such as #28415F or use the colour square. The app warns if the text contrast would be hard to read.
  4. Rename the six location levels, from largest to smallest, and choose which level is the “site” level (it carries the address, year built, climate zone and the PM wizard).
  5. Optionally change the word “household” (to organization, say).
  6. Select “Save branding”, or “Reset to defaults” to undo your changes.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Name * — The app’s name, shown at the top of the menu and on the sign-in screen.
  • 2Short name — A short form used in small spaces.
  • 3Tagline — Line shown under the name.
  • 4Top-bar title (optional) — If filled, shown in the top bar.
  • 5Logo — The image beside the name. The square to the left previews the current one.
  • 6Primary (light mode) — Main colour (menu background, headings) when the app is in light mode.
  • 7Accent (light mode) — Highlight colour (buttons, badges) in light mode.
  • 8Primary (dark mode) — Main colour in dark mode.
  • 9Accent (dark mode) — Highlight colour in dark mode.
  • 10Location levels 1–6 — The names of the six location levels, largest first. Each is required, up to 15 characters, and all must differ.
  • 11Site level — Which level is the property that carries address, year built, climate zone and the PM wizard.
  • 12Word for “household” — Replaces the word wherever the app says household.
  • 13Save branding / Reset to defaults — Save applies the changes; Reset restores the original look.

Tools and settings: Features

Features switches optional parts of the app on or off. Changes take effect immediately. Nothing is deleted when something is switched off; it is simply hidden.

What to do

  1. Tick “Home Assistant alarms” to enable the webhook, sensor mappings and the Alarms page.
  2. Tick “Fill in from a link” to show the paste-a-link helper on asset, vendor and part forms; tick “Use AI (Gemini)” beneath it to improve results (needs a key set on the server).
  3. Tick “Execution-based scheduling and time keeping” to rename Schedule to Labour assignment and add estimates, crews, multiple executors, week and day views and hours worked.
  4. Tick “Workforce scheduling” to add the Workforce schedule tab.
  5. Tick “Hourly labour assignments” to add the 30-minute grid to the day view. It is available only when the two scheduling features above are both on.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Home Assistant alarms — Turns the sensor webhook and Alarms page on or off.
  • 2Fill in from a link — Turns the paste-a-link helper on or off.
  • 3Use AI (Gemini) — Optional AI refinement of filled-in values.
  • 4Execution-based scheduling and time keeping — Labour assignment, estimates, crews, hours worked.
  • 5Workforce scheduling — Adds the Workforce schedule tab, shift templates and PDF export.
  • 6Hourly labour assignments — 30-minute grid in the day view; needs both of the above.
  • 7Emailed password reset status — Shows whether people can reset their own password by email.

Tools and settings: Backup and bulk edit

Everything in the app can be exported to an Excel workbook or a full backup file, edited in bulk, and imported again. The app also keeps its own automatic nightly snapshots.

What to do

  1. “Export to Excel” downloads a workbook with one sheet per kind of record. Edit rows (including bulk changes) and re-import it, or keep it as a backup.
  2. “Full backup” downloads a .zip with the workbook and all photos.
  3. “Import from Excel or backup…” asks for a file, checks it, and lets you choose which tabs to apply. If anything is wrong you get an error log and nothing changes.
  4. Tick “Include login credentials” only if you want password hashes and the webhook key in the export; leave it off for files you will share.
  5. Automatic snapshots are taken about once a day and the latest seven are kept. Download one, or select “Take a snapshot now”. They live on the same disk as the app, so also keep your own Full backup elsewhere.
  6. “Shrink existing photos” reduces the size of photos uploaded before automatic shrinking was added.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Export to Excel — Downloads all records as a workbook.
  • 2Full backup (.zip, with photos) — Downloads everything including photos.
  • 3Import from Excel or backup… — Pre-checks a file and applies the tabs you choose.
  • 4Include login credentials — Adds password hashes and the alarm webhook key to exports. Leave off unless you need a complete restore.
  • 5Automatic database snapshots — The seven most recent nightly copies, each with date, time and size and a Download link.
  • 6Take a snapshot now — Makes a snapshot immediately, for example before a big edit.
  • 7Shrink existing photos — One-off clean-up that reduces older photos to the standard size.

Tools and settings: PM Wizard starter catalogue

The starter catalogue is the list of about 300 suggested maintenance jobs offered by the PM setup wizard. Edit it to match your household — remove what never applies, change intervals, add your own. Editing the catalogue never changes PM Bases that were already created. (Only the first few entries are shown here; the real list is long.)

What to do

  1. Narrow the list with the Type and Sub type boxes or the search box.
  2. Use the pencil on a row to edit it and the red bin to remove it.
  3. Select “View entries” to open the list, then “Add an entry” to add your own (next page).
  4. “Reset to default” restores the original catalogue (your edits are lost).

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Reset to default — Restores the built-in catalogue.
  • 2Add entry — Adds a new suggested job.
  • 3Type filter — Home or Facilities (and any types you add).
  • 4Sub type filter — Category within the type (HVAC & Heating, Plumbing & Water …).
  • 5Search — Find an entry by name.
  • 6Count — How many entries match the filters.
  • 7Catalogue entry — Title, then type · sub type · repeat interval · climate zones, then a note. Pencil edits; bin removes.

Tools and settings: adding or editing a catalogue entry

Each catalogue entry becomes a PM Base when someone ticks it in the wizard.

What to do

  1. Enter or choose the Type and Sub type (a new name creates a new group).
  2. Type the Title and an optional Description.
  3. Set how often it repeats with Every and Unit.
  4. Leave “Applies to all climate zones” ticked, or untick it and choose the zones where it makes sense.
  5. Select Save.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Type — Home, Facilities or your own type.
  • 2Sub type — Category within the type.
  • 3Title * — Becomes the PM Base title.
  • 4Description — Note shown in the wizard and copied to the PM Base.
  • 5Every / Unit — Repeat interval.
  • 6Applies to all climate zones — Untick to limit the entry to chosen climate zones; others are greyed out in the wizard.
  • 7Save / Cancel — Save stores the entry.

Tools and settings: Delete a work order or request

Normally a mistaken work order or request is declined or closed so the record is kept. If one was created in error and must disappear completely, an Owner can delete it here by number or title. This is permanent.

What to do

  1. Type the number (WO-0012, WR-0004) or part of the title in the box.
  2. Select the matching result and confirm.
  3. Deleting a PM Base removes the template; jobs generated from it stay but no more are created. A request linked to a deleted work order simply loses the link.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Delete a work order — Search by number or title (also works for PM Base templates).
  • 2Delete a work request — Search by number or title.

Scheduling and time keeping (optional)

How scheduling and time keeping work

Three optional switches

Your Owner can switch on three optional features in Tools > Features: Execution-based scheduling (labour assignment and hours worked), Workforce scheduling (who works when) and Hourly assignment (a 30-minute grid inside each day). Hourly needs the other two. With all three off the app looks and behaves as in earlier versions.

Estimate, crew and executors

On a work order enter Estimated hours (per person), Crew required (how many people at once) and one or more executors. The first executor listed remains the primary executor for filters and reports.

Labour assignment

The Schedule page becomes Labour assignment. Drag a work order onto a day (or an hour) to schedule it, and drag a person’s name onto a work order to assign them. A day that is short of people for the crew required is flagged as under-staffed.

Workforce schedule

A calendar of who is working when. Drag a person onto a week or a day, then choose a shift template or enter a one-time shift. When you edit a shift enter any two of start, duration and end and the third is calculated. An end time earlier than the start means an overnight shift, shown on the day it starts. Each day header shows first start, last end and any gap in coverage (in red).

Hours worked

When an executor completes a work order they are asked how many hours they worked. Hours appear on the work order, in Tools > My hours and, for managers, in Tools > Hours worked.

Touch screens

On a tablet or phone, tap a work order card or a person’s name to pick it up (it is highlighted and a banner shows what you are holding), then tap the day, person’s day, week box or hour slot where it should go. Tap Cancel or the held card again to put it down, or Open to see the work order.

PDF

Both planning calendars have a Print / PDF button that exports the visible month, week or day.

Labour assignment: month view

Labour assignment is the Schedule renamed when execution-based scheduling is on. Use it to decide who does which work and when. The month view shows each week in its own box, with the ISO week number on the left.

What to do

  1. Use the arrows to change month; the up arrow is disabled here because this is the top level.
  2. Select a day number to open that day, or the week number to open that week.
  3. Drag a work order from the side list onto a day to schedule it for that day. Then open the week or day view to give it people.
  4. Use the executor and location filters to focus on part of the work.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Back and forward — Previous and next month.
  • 2Month / Week / Day — Jumps directly to a view.
  • 3Location filter — Show only work at one place and everything inside it.
  • 4Executor filter — Tick one or more people; blank shows everyone.
  • 5Week header — ISO week number. Select it to open the week view.
  • 6Day box — Work scheduled that day. Select the number to open the day. Coloured dots show who is assigned; a dashed red outline means not enough people.
  • 7Work orders to place — Open work orders by due date. Drag one onto a day.

Editing or deleting a shift

On the Workforce schedule, tap any shift chip to edit it. The pop-up lets you change the start, duration and end (fill any two) or pick a daily template, and has a Delete shift button. There is no small x on the chips any more.

What to do

  1. Tap a shift on the Workforce schedule.
  2. Change the times, or choose a template.
  3. Select Save, or Delete shift to remove it.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Who and when — The person and the day of the shift.
  • 2Delete — Removes this shift from the schedule.

Labour assignment: week view

The week view has one board per person with a column for each day, and an Unassigned board for work with nobody on it yet. Each column header shows that person's total scheduled hours for the day.

What to do

  1. Drag a work order from the side list onto a person's day to add that person to it and schedule it for that day.
  2. Drag a card from one person to another to move it. Use the small x on a card to take it off that person.
  3. Select a day header to open the day view.
  4. A person only has a column for days they are on shift when Workforce scheduling is on; days off are greyed.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1A person's board — Their name, their hours for the week and a column for each day.
  • 2Day header — Day and total estimated hours for this person that day. Select it to open the day.
  • 3Work order card — Title, people needed (person icon), hours each (clock icon). “Short” with a dashed red outline means more people are needed.
  • 4Unassigned work — Scheduled work that has no person yet. Drag its card to a person.
  • 5Off day — Greyed: not on shift that day (Workforce scheduling on).

Labour assignment: day view

The day view has one column for each person working that day, plus Unassigned. All columns fit on one screen. It is the place to balance a day's workload.

What to do

  1. Drag work orders from the side list onto a person's column.
  2. Check each header's hours against the length of the shift.
  3. A work order that needs several people appears in several columns; add a person by dragging it onto another column.
  4. Use the up arrow to go back to the week.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Up arrow — Day to Week.
  • 2Person header — Name in their colour and total estimated hours that day.
  • 3Card with crew and hours — Person icon: people needed. Clock icon: hours each.
  • 4Unassigned column — Work on this day with nobody assigned yet.
  • 5Work orders to place — Drag from here onto a column.

Labour assignment: hourly day view

When Hourly labour assignments is on (it needs both scheduling features), each person's column becomes a grid of 30-minute slots that follows their shift. Drag a card to the slot where the work should start and it stretches to the length of the task.

What to do

  1. Drag a card from the side list, or from the “No start time” strip, onto a slot inside the person's shift.
  2. Slots outside the shift are shaded and cannot be used.
  3. Drag a card to a new slot to change its start time; drop it on the “No start time” strip to clear the time.
  4. Overlapping cards sit side by side.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1No start time strip — Cards for the day that have no time yet.
  • 2Hour grid — 30-minute slots from the earliest shift start to the latest end. Shaded slots are outside this person's shift.
  • 3Placed card — Starts in its slot and is as tall as its estimated hours.
  • 4Another person's grid — Each person's shaded and unshaded slots follow their own shift.

Work orders: executors, estimate and crew

With execution-based scheduling on, the work order form lets you assign several executors, estimate the time and say how many people are needed. The same fields appear when you edit a work order.

What to do

  1. Tap the names to choose one or more executors; a tick shows who is chosen.
  2. Enter the estimated hours per executor.
  3. Enter how many executors are required. If fewer are assigned than required, the work order is flagged on Labour assignment.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Executors — Tap a name to add or remove that person.
  • 2Hours per executor — How long one person needs. A two-person job of 3 hours each is 6 hours of labour.
  • 3Executors required — How many people the job needs (default 1).

Hours worked prompt

When any work order is completed with execution-based scheduling on, the person completing it enters hours for each assigned executor (or for themselves if nobody is assigned). Totals appear on Tools under “Hours worked — all executors”.

What to do

  1. Open the work order and choose Completed.
  2. Enter hours for each executor.
  3. Select Complete.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Hours per executor — Required and greater than 0.
  • 2Complete — Saves the hours as time entries and completes the work order.

Workforce schedule: month view

The Workforce schedule is where managers set who is working when. Everyone can view it. Name cards for the team sit across the top; drag one onto a day or onto a week number to schedule that person.

What to do

  1. Drag a name card onto a day to schedule one day, or onto the week number box to schedule a whole week.
  2. Choose a template in the window that appears, or set a one-time schedule (next pages).
  3. Remove a shift with the small x on it.
  4. Select Export PDF to print the schedule, or Create new template to go to Tools.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Name cards — One per person, in their colour. They stay where they are so you can use them again.
  • 2Create new template — Opens Tools at the Shift templates card.
  • 3Export PDF — Printable page of the month, week or day on screen.
  • 4Week header (drop zone) — Drop a name card here to schedule a whole week. Select it to open the week.
  • 5Day box — Shifts that day. Select the number to open the day.
  • 6Day hours — First start and last end of the day. Red means a gap in coverage; hover to see when.
  • 7Overnight shift — A shift that ends before it starts runs overnight and is shown on the day it starts (the +1 means it ends the next day).

Workforce schedule: week view

The week view lists the shifts for each day of one week. The left-hand box carries the week number and is where a name card is dropped to schedule the whole week.

What to do

  1. Drop a name card on a day column for one day, or on the week box for the week.
  2. Check each day's times in red or grey at the top.
  3. Use the arrows to move week by week.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Week box — Drop a name card here for the whole week.
  • 2Day column — That day's shifts, earliest first.
  • 3Gap warning — Red times: nobody works between 11:00 and 13:00 on this day. Hover to read the explanation.

Workforce schedule: day view

The day view shows each person's shift for the day in their column, with the day's coverage at the top.

What to do

  1. Drop a name card anywhere on the day to schedule that person for the day.
  2. Use the arrows to go to the next or previous day.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Coverage — First start to last end. Red when part of that time has nobody working.
  • 2A person's column — Their shift for the day, or “Not scheduled”.

Scheduling a person: choosing a template

After you drop a name card on a day, this window asks which shift to apply. Dropping on a week box offers weekly templates instead. The person's existing shifts on those days are replaced.

What to do

  1. Select a saved template to apply it straight away.
  2. Or select “One-time daily schedule…” (or weekly) for a schedule you will not reuse.
  3. Check the schedule and change it if needed.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Saved template — Name and times. Selecting it applies it at once.
  • 2One-time schedule — Opens a form to set the shift just for this drop.

Scheduling a person: a one-time schedule

A one-time schedule lets you set an unusual shift without making a template. You can still save it as a template for next time.

What to do

  1. Fill in any two of start, duration and end.
  2. Optionally type a name to save it as a template.
  3. Select Apply.

Numbered items in the picture

  • 1Start / duration / end — Fill in any two; the third is calculated.
  • 2Save as a template — Optional name. Leave blank to use the schedule only once.
  • 3Apply — Schedules the person on the chosen day(s).

Glossary

TermMeaning
Active / Scheduled / Completed / ClosedThe four stages of a work order. See Key ideas.
AlarmAn alert that needs attention: from a sensor (Home Assistant), an out-of-range checklist reading, or entered by hand. Managers and owners handle alarms.
ArchiveThe list of all Closed work orders, reached from the Closed column.
AssetA piece of equipment or an item worth maintaining (furnace, fridge, mower).
BenchmarkA saved reference procedure and cost for a kind of job, copied onto new Corrective work orders.
BOM (Bill of Materials)The tree of components, sub-components and parts that make up an asset.
ChecklistThe steps on a PM work order; steps may be ticks, readings, photos or pass/fail.
Climate zoneA setting on the property (Very Cold … Marine) that scales the starter PM catalogue.
CorrectiveA work order type: a planned repair.
ExecutorRole (and a field on a work order): the person who does the work.
Fixed / Non-fixedPM modes. Fixed repeats on the same calendar date(s) each year; Non-fixed repeats a set interval after the last completion.
LocationA place in the household tree: property, structure, floor, room, area. The words are configurable.
MeterA usage counter on an asset (hours, kilometres) used by meter-based PM.
PM / PM BasePreventive maintenance: a PM is one job; a PM Base is the repeating template that generates them.
PriorityLow, Medium, High or Critical.
QR labelA printable label whose QR code opens the asset’s record.
Required byThe deadline for a request or work order. Work past it is flagged Overdue.
Reorder levelThe stock level at or below which a part is flagged Reorder.
Crew requiredHow many people a work order needs at the same time. Used by the planning calendars to flag an under-staffed day.
Estimated hoursHow long a work order is expected to take per person. Used for hourly scheduling and to compare with hours worked.
Executor colourThe colour each executor is shown in on the planning calendars.
Hours workedTime recorded against a work order by an executor when it is completed; totals appear in Tools.
Info button (i)A small round button beside a title that opens a short explanation: what the area is for, how to use it and who can.
Overnight shiftA shift whose end time is earlier than its start time. It ends the next day but is always shown on the day it starts.
Shift templateA saved daily or weekly shift pattern that can be dropped onto a person and a day or week on the Workforce schedule.
StandbyA pause on a PM Base, by hand or outside a yearly window.
Work requestA report that something needs attention, awaiting review by a manager or owner.
Work orderA job to be done, with who, what, where, when, parts and cost.
